- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or adjust downward by 3–8% in next 5 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model often overreacts; apply downward bias of 3–7% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) and price is volatile; add 1–3% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence; if below, add 1–3% per day.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag by 1–3 days; adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days if sentiment is bullish.
- When sentiment drops sharply after a spike, model fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days if sentiment <0.2.
